value.rationale: The 2019 dyadic-line Toeplitz example motivates a natural infinite-scale sampling measure but only a nonsharp 2^{-2j} sufficient regime. The claim finds the exact beta=1 boundary, the sharp and strictly unattained embedding constant and its single maximizing phase, with nonvanishing high-frequency log ripple. This is a natural exact operator norm and critical threshold used to calibrate singular Carleson trace inequalities, not an arbitrary parameter slice or table recomputation. Despite the tiny numerical oscillation, exact nonattainment and extremal rigidity are structurally meaningful. The additional exact equality of norms for the one-sided and two-sided stacks shows that removing infinitely many coarse sampling lines has no effect on the sharp norm, even though it strictly lowers every nonzero quadratic form value.
